newsitem.title: UK: Labour plan won't impress UK markets-Clarke.
newsitem.headline: Labour plan won't impress UK markets-Clarke.

text.p: The opposition Labour party's plans to keep inflation down and reform Britain's monetary policy-making procedures are "political flannel" that will not impress the financial markets, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday.
"It is not the case that anybody in the money markets is going to be impressed by this posturing," Clarke told BBC radio.
Labour economics spokesman Gordon Brown will set out his policies in the two key areas in a speech at 1800 gmt.

But he has already said he would come to his decisions after taking advice from a broad-based monetary policy committee in the Bank of England, and from a new Council of Economic Advisers within the Treasury.
Clarke said this would lead to a Labour Chancellor of the Exchequer taking "politicised decisions" after receiving advice behind closed doors.
"He wants to retreat back into the old system in which the Chancellor takes a decision based on advice which is closed from the outside world," Clarke said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
